activities.anchor: The biological approach earns its claims
activities.caption: sort each method into its causal route
activities.name: bhvRouteBuckets

config.prompt: Correlational, interventional or hormonal? File each method or finding by the causal route it runs:

items.label: twin designs partitioning variance into heritability and environment
brain imaging associations between structure and behaviour
optogenetics switching neurons on and off with light in freely moving mice
block a receptor, observe the behaviour change
the HPA axis releasing cortisol in a slow cascade
Sapolsky's baboons: subordinate males with elevated baseline cortisol, stress measured in the wild

config.why: Every claim in the chapter leans on one of the three routes, and the critical skill is knowing which — lesions, receptor blocks and light-controlled neurons prove necessity; scans and twins only associate.

activities.anchor: The results that shaped the field
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a twin-study briefing
activities.name: bhvTwinSpot

config.prompt: One line of this twin-study briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Identical (monozygotic) twins share essentially all their genes; fraternal (dizygotic) pairs share about half.
Reared-apart designs, like the Minnesota studies of Bouchard and colleagues, add environment to the subtraction.
No trait sits at 100% heritability — genes and environment always both at work.
Phenylketonuria is the textbook proof that a genetic disorder can never be modified once diagnosed.
config.correction: Phenylketonuria is a textbook genetic disorder controlled entirely by diet — the standing proof that a biological basis and a modifiable outcome are compatible.
config.why: 'Genetic' never means 'unalterable', and heritability is a population statistic: it says nothing about an individual and changes with the population's environmental range.

activities.caption: true or false — genes and plasticity
activities.name: bhvGeneJudge

statements.s: No serious version of the biological approach claims everything is genetic.
statements.why: Heritability is always population-specific and never implies immutability; the field's strongest findings are interactions.

statements.s: Meaney's rat work showed maternal licking and grooming stably alters glucocorticoid-receptor methylation in offspring.
statements.why: Experience altering gene expression — epigenetics — is one of the interactions the approach leads with.

statements.s: The biological approach's strongest findings are main effects of genes acting alone.
statements.why: The opposite: genes modulating sensitivity to environments, hormones responding to social ranks, experience altering gene expression.

statements.s: Biology is the substrate of plasticity, not its enemy.
statements.why: Which is why the next section spends its time on experiments rather than on nature-versus-nurture verdicts.

activities.caption: order the Dement and Kleitman procedure
activities.name: bhvRemOrder

config.prompt: The 1957 REM study, procedure first — order the steps:
items: Sleep in a laboratory wired with EEG electrodes and eye-movement recording
A bell wakes the sleeper at scheduled and random points — sometimes during REM, sometimes during NREM
Report into a recorder whether you were dreaming
Compare dream reports against the sleep state that was recorded
Check the graded relations: recall tracking REM duration, eye-movement direction matching reported content
config.why: Wake the sleeper, ask, compare against physiology — the method converted dreaming from unfalsifiable anecdote into a measurable physiological state, and it is still the template for sleep science.

activities.anchor: The 2013 discovery of the glymphatic system
activities.caption: scrub the dated landmarks of the lesson
activities.name: bhvDatesTimeline

events.title: REM is discovered
events.text: Aserinsky and Kleitman find rapid eye movement sleep — the physiological state the 1957 study would tie to dreaming.

events.title: Rats press for reward
events.text: Olds and Milner discover rats will press a lever for hours to stimulate the dopamine pathway — the reward field begins.

events.title: Dement and Kleitman
events.text: Roughly 80% of REM awakenings produce dream recall against about 7% in NREM — subjective experience gains a readable bodily correlate.

events.title: Maguire's taxi drivers
events.text: London taxi drivers who acquired 'the Knowledge' show measurably larger posterior hippocampi, volume tracking years of driving.

events.title: Hölzel's mindfulness scans
events.text: Sixteen adults before and after an eight-week MBSR course: grey-matter increases in several regions, decreases in the right basolateral amygdala.

events.title: The glymphatic system
events.text: Cerebrospinal fluid is found flushing metabolic waste through brain tissue, dramatically more active during sleep — sleep gains a physical maintenance function.

activities.anchor: ran the clean control: rhesus monkeys
activities.caption: drag the divider — the two findings side by side
activities.name: bhvToyCompare

config.prompt: Hassett, Siebert and Wallen (2008): thirty-four rhesus monkeys, trucks and plush toys, contact time scored per monkey — drag the divider.

before.label: males
before.text: Preferentially interacted with the wheeled toys — paralleling the human pattern in which boys favour wheeled toys from around age two.

after.label: females
after.text: More variable: spent more time with both toy types, without a consistent plush preference — the finding the headlines ignored.

config.why: Because these animals had no gendered upbringing, the difference points to prenatal hormonal (androgen-mediated) contributions — the controlled cross-species comparison that separates biology from culture.

config.q: The monkey study found a sex difference in toy contact with no human socialisation. Which sentence is the prudent reading?
choices: Gendered toy preferences are hardwired in humans
Toy preferences are purely socialised — biology plays no part
Biology may bias initial interests; human gender socialisation then amplifies them enormously
The study proved females strongly prefer plush toys
config.why: Both prudent sentences are supported — a biological contribution to a specific preference, in another species, under one set of conditions, and no consistent female plush preference. Biology biases; socialisation amplifies; only the hardwired version makes headlines.

activities.anchor: scanned sixteen adults before and after
activities.caption: pair each scan region with what changed
activities.name: bhvHolzelMatch

config.prompt: Hölzel and colleagues (2011): pair each element of the design with its result or caveat:

pairs.right: grey-matter concentration increased — a region tied to learning and memory
grey-matter concentration decreased, tracking each person's self-reported stress reduction

pairs.left: posterior cingulate, temporo-parietal junction and cerebellum
pairs.right: the other regions that increased alongside the hippocampus
seventeen scan-matched participants who did no alternative activity — expectation and attention effects uncontrolled

config.why: A structural change from eight weeks of practice, consistent with experience-dependent plasticity — but the sample was tiny, the controls inactive and later replications mixed: suggestive, not conclusive, and that is the honest teaching point.
